title: Matrices indexed by arbitrary sets
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $I,J$ be sets (finite or infinite). An $I\times J$ matrix with entries in $R$ is a family $A=(a_{ij})_{i\in I,\,j\in J}$ of elements $a_{ij}\in R$, i.e. a function $I\times J\to R$; $a_{ij}$ is its entry in row $i$ and column $j$. For $I=\{1,\ldots,m\}$, $J=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ this is an $m\times n$ matrix; for $I=J=\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ it is an infinite matrix $(a_{rs})_{r,s\geq0}$.
